page: The Hetzner Cloud cx23 is an entry-level virtual server powered by the QEMU hypervisor. It features an x86_64 Intel Xeon CPU with 2 shared vCPUs running at 2.0 GHz, 4.0 GB of system memory, and 40 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The processor includes a cache configuration of 32 KB L1d, 4 MB L2, and 16 MB L3, alongside support for instruction sets such as AVX, AVX512F, AES, and FMA. No complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included with this instance.

Performance benchmarks place this instance consistently in the lower tiers. Single-core and multi-core CPU tests, such as stress-ng and Geekbench, rank in the bottom 10% of tested hardware. Memory bandwidth is limited, with read-only large block transfers reaching 20.91 GB/sec and write operations at 16.93 GB/sec. Cryptographic, database, and compression benchmarks also reflect entry-level performance, with Redis SET operations executing at 2.52 million operations per second and static web serving throughput at 1.77 GB/sec.

Due to its shared CPU allocation and modest hardware profile, the cx23 is highly cost-efficient for low-demand applications where continuous high performance is not required. It is best suited for lightweight workloads such as basic web serving, development environments, small utility scripts, and minor background tasks. It is not suitable for resource-intensive databases, large-scale LLM inference, or high-throughput computing.
